reason: Select Andrew Glasgow-1239 as the possible working father of Alexander Glasgow-3612. The inspected 17 April 1757 Mid Calder transcript names Alexander, father Andrew Glasgow and mother Janet Young. The adult Alexander’s uncertain 1760 birth and Newton/Midlothian family are compatible with this child: a 1757 child would be about 20 at his son George’s reported 1777 birth. The three-year difference from an uncertain birth field is not an exclusion. Andrew-1239’s 21 December 1729 Livingston baptism places a documented Andrew in the neighbouring parish and the right generation, aged about 27 in 1757. This is the preferred available regional and chronological reconstruction, rather than leaving the named-parent lead entirely outside the working tree.
scope: 42% is a subjective assessment of the complete adult Alexander → Andrew-1239 profile pair, including both the 1757 child-to-adult identification and the identification of the named Andrew with the Livingston child. Neither identity is proved by a shared occupation, witness, holding or later parent clause. The record-defined father’s given name and surname are explicit; that does not make this later profile pair confident. Andrew-3052, associated with Janet Clerk and an earlier Alexander household, remains an unselected possible alternative at 32%; a different spouse is not an exclusion. Other or unrepresented Andrews remain possible. No percentages are multiplied, and the two Andrew hypotheses are not independent propositions. Janet Young is the recorded mother but no modern mother identity is assigned. All vital fields, spouses and existing child links remain unchanged.
